Package org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.agentic

Class AgenticAdHocParseListener

java.lang.Object
org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.bpmn.parser.AbstractBpmnParseListener
org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.agentic.AgenticAdHocParseListener
All Implemented Interfaces:
BpmnParseListener
public class AgenticAdHocParseListener extends AbstractBpmnParseListener
Turns an agentic ad hoc sub process into one whose turns are driven by a job: parks it, records its configuration, and attaches what schedules the turns: a start listener and a trigger the scope's behaviour tells of every child that ends.

A scope is agentic when it carries the AI agent's connector, camunda:connector with the id cibseven-ai-agent -- the same element and the same input parameters as an AI agent service task, evaluated on every turn instead of once. Only the agent's limits and settings stay properties of the scope.

Every other trace of an agent on a sub process -- the agent's element template, its limits and settings, its connector on the wrong element -- without a scope the agent can run refuses the deployment, saying why and what to do. A modeler drops a connector it does not expect on a sub process when the element is copied or its type is changed; without this check such a scope would deploy as a plain ad hoc scope and wait for ever.

In every process it parses, agentic or not, it also refuses a call of the expression function toolParameter that no agentic scope reads (CIB7-2136): the function resolves on every engine, and such a call would deploy and fail when it runs.

Of an AI agent service task it only records the names of the connector's output parameters, for the agent's response to find the AI-output marker among them (CIB7-2819).

Each of these refuses a new deployment only. A definition parsed again from a deployment made while the agent was off, after a restart, a cache eviction or on another node, is not refused: that would stop every instance of it. Its refusals are logged instead, and it loads without what they refuse: a scope no agent can run as the plain scope it was deployed as, a broken tool or setting left out (CIB7-2136, CIB7-2367). A check added after a release leaves out the part, never the agent: see AgenticToolCatalogParser.Parsing.

Registered as a post parse listener. It needs the behaviour, the children and their sequence flows, none of which exist while the scope is being built.

    • recordInterruptions

      protected static void recordInterruptions(ActivityImpl child)
      Makes child, a child of an agentic scope, record how it interrupted a tool's flow, if it is an interrupting boundary event of a kind that does (see AgenticToolEndRecorder for where the recorder sits). A boundary error event's definition on the activity it is attached to is replaced by one that remembers the code it caught; the engine hands the code to the event only through a process variable the modeller has to ask for (see AgenticCaughtError). An activity with boundary events of other kinds only gets a watch, which catches nothing and notes an error that found no handler. A non-interrupting event ends nothing, and the engine refuses one inside an ad hoc sub process anyway (CIB7-1967); a compensation or cancel event is not one the agent's tools are ended by.

    • withoutAgentsLoadedPlain

      protected static List<AdHocToolDescriptor> withoutAgentsLoadedPlain(Element scopeElement, ActivityImpl activity, List<AdHocToolDescriptor> catalog, AgenticToolCatalogParser.Parsing parsing)
      The catalogue without a tool that reaches a nested ad hoc scope that asks for an agent but loads without one, as a parse again leaves it plain (CIB7-2367): the tool itself, a scope inside it, or one its flow leads to. Such a scope starts nothing on entry and no turn ends it, so the tool would never end, and the agent here could not end its own scope while it is pending. A deployment never keeps one: that scope refuses it first. Children are parsed before their scope, so whether a nested scope has its agent is known here.

      A nested scope that has its agent is its own: what is inside it is left to its catalogue. An AI agent task is no scope and needs none, and a plain sub process runs to its end on its own. An agent behind a call activity is in another definition, not known here.

    • refuseABadDeclarationOfProcessVariables

      protected void refuseABadDeclarationOfProcessVariables(Element scopeElement, ActivityImpl activity, Map<String,String> inputs)
      contextVariables is plain text, and names each variable once, and none of the agent's own state (CIB7-2179). A list, a map or a script has no text to read once. An empty name is a stray comma, and a name declared twice a slip of the pen; either would leave a modeller wondering what the agent sees. A name with $, braces, a semicolon or an asterisk, or one longer than a variable's name can be, is an expression, a list or a pattern written by habit and would never match. A name with a space inside is a comma left out far more often than a name, and ${…} could not read such a name anyway. The agent's own state is kept from the model on every path, and a declaration would hand it out.

      optionalContextVariables is checked the same way. A name in it that contextVariables does not declare is no refusal: it only modifies that list, so the name is ignored with a warning when the scope is parsed, as on the AI agent task (CIB7-1843).

      protected static IoMapping connectorInputOutput(Element connector)
      The connector's input and output mapping as BpmnParseUtil.parseInputOutput(org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.util.xml.Element) builds it, without CONTEXT_VARIABLES and OPTIONAL_CONTEXT_VARIABLES: those two are names, read once as text (declarationInputs(org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.util.xml.Element)), and never built as expressions, so no step evaluates them. Built, a ${…} written into them by habit would be an error of the connector: the whole agent refused for what only its declaration got wrong, or, for a function this node lacks, the definition not loaded at all (the second model's review of 14637f31c5). null without an inputOutput, as there.

    • parsing

      protected static AgenticToolCatalogParser.Parsing parsing(ProcessDefinitionImpl definition)
      This parse of the definition, for every check of the agent (CIB7-2136, CIB7-2367): its process, as the modeller named it, and whether it is deployed now or parsed again from a deployment made earlier. The engine marks a deployment it parses again as not new, on the very entity it reads in the same command, before it parses it (ResourceDefinitionCache); a new one carries the mark from its deployment. Outside a command, as when a model is only validated, it counts as a deployment.

      A definition parsed again is named in the log by its version, id, deployment and tenant, so an operator finds which one to correct. The version is not parsed but stored, so it is read only when something is logged.

    • parseProcess

      public void parseProcess(Element processElement, ProcessDefinitionEntity processDefinition)
      An agentic scope with onLimit = error needs a boundary error event on it for every limit it can reach (CIB7-2151). The engine ends an execution without a word when nothing catches a BPMN error (enableExceptionsAfterUnhandledBpmnError is off by default), so a limit no boundary event catches would end the scope with no trace in the process; and an error event sub process inside the scope that catches the limit takes it before any boundary event can. Checked here, once the whole process is parsed and its boundary events are known. On a parse again ON_LIMIT is left out of such a scope instead (CIB7-2367): a limit then ends it as any turn would.

      Also here: a tool parameter declared where no agentic scope reads it, outside every agentic scope, refuses the deployment (CIB7-2136), since the function resolves on every engine.

      Specified by:
      parseProcess in interface BpmnParseListener
      Overrides:
      parseProcess in class AbstractBpmnParseListener

    • firstHandler

      protected static ActivityImpl firstHandler(ProcessDefinitionEntity definition, ActivityImpl scope, String code)
      The handler the engine gives the code to when the scope throws it, or null when none on the scope catches it: the first of the scope's error handlers that catches the code, as ErrorDeclarationForProcessInstanceFinder picks it. The list holds the boundary error events on the scope and the error start events of the event sub processes inside it, sorted by precedence; an event sub process ranks above every boundary event, whatever their codes. An AgenticCaughtError is asked through AgenticCaughtError.matches(java.lang.String), so the check notes no caught code.

      protected void refuseTheTaskOnTheScope(Element scopeElement, ActivityImpl activity)
      The agent reads its task and prompt from its connector. The same input parameter on the scope itself is refused: it would be evaluated once, on entry, into a variable any child can rewrite, and the agent would never see it.

    • refuseAnImpossibleConversation

      protected void refuseAnImpossibleConversation(Element scopeElement, ScopeImpl scope, ActivityImpl activity, Map<String,String> properties)
      What the conversation settings of CIB7-2137 cannot mean, refused at deployment rather than on the first turn of the first instance.

      Four things: a mode that is not one of the two; a total turn limit on a scope whose entries share no conversation, where it would bound nothing a per-entry limit does not bound already; that same limit when it is not a positive integer; and a continued conversation on a parallel multi-instance scope, whose instances run at once and would write one conversation concurrently — the losers fail with an OptimisticLockingException and replay a model call each. Sequential multi-instance iterations share the conversation and total cap; later iterations are re-entries and use followUp on their first turn.
